claims.text: The FDA darunavir label lists colchicine under anti-gout drugs and says co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal and/or hepatic impairment because of potential serious or life-threatening reactions.
claims.quote: Co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal and/or hepatic impairment due to potential for serious and/or life-threatening reactions.

claims.text: The FDA colchicine label says use with P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, including all protease inhibitors except fosamprenavir, is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment.
claims.quote: Use of colchicine tablets in conjunction with P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (this includes all protease inhibitors except fosamprenavir) is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment

claims.text: The French darunavir label says concomitant use of colchicine and boosted darunavir may increase colchicine exposure.
claims.quote: L’utilisation concomitante de la colchicine et de darunavir boosté peut augmenter l’exposition à la colchicine.
claims.quoteEnglish: Concomitant use of colchicine and boosted darunavir may increase colchicine exposure.

headline.text: The FDA darunavir label contraindicates co-administration with colchicine in patients with renal and/or hepatic impairment (c1).

reported.text: The FDA colchicine label extends its contraindication in renal or hepatic impairment to all protease inhibitors except fosamprenavir.
The French darunavir label says boosted darunavir may increase colchicine exposure.

gaps.text: No controlled human study of this combination was found in the PubMed search.
